teenKit.tldr: An anatomical MRI is just an expensive, high-resolution photograph that can look totally normal while your brain's software is crashing. To find invisible neurological disorders, doctors have to use real-time electrical wiretapping and chemical assays.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It proves that the most terrifying and complex medical mysteries can't be solved by simply taking a picture of the body, requiring entirely different ways of listening to our internal electrical grid.
keyTakeaways: An MRI shows physical structure like a photograph, but it is completely blind to microscopic electrical failures or misfolded proteins.
Neurological testing acts like a live wiretap on the body's electrical grid to catch problems in real-time.
Advanced assays can detect invisible chemical anomalies, such as cascading misfolded proteins, long before they show up on standard structural scans.
